original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume h < m <= p. Is the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset of an m-element subset always min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}? In other words, does rho_hat(G, m, h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1} hold throughout this range?
target_in_paper: Section 0.3, Conjecture 0.3.3: the paper’s specific open problem asserting the finite-abelian-group analogue of the prime-order restricted-sumset formula in the range h < m <= p.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content of the paper’s target statement: it uses the right ambient class (finite abelian groups), the right parameter p (the smallest prime divisor of |G|), the right range h < m <= p, and the right conjectural formula min{p, hm - h^2 + 1} for the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset.
missing_details: The paper formally defines rho_hat(G,m,h) as the minimum of |h^∧A| over all m-element subsets A of G; that definition should be included explicitly to make the question stand-alone.
The paper defines h^∧A as the h-fold restricted sumset, i.e. the set of sums of h distinct elements of A; this operator should be spelled out.

The quantifiers should be explicit: the question is whether the formula holds for every finite abelian group G of order n and every pair of integers h,m with h < m <= p, where p is the smallest prime divisor of n.
The group is written additively in the paper; while standard, stating this removes ambiguity.
The paper presents this as a conjecture/open problem, not as an established theorem; the refined version should preserve that status.

The paper frames this statement specifically as the restricted-sumset analogue of the prime-order result in Theorem 0.3.1, so the rewritten question should stay narrowly on this formula and not drift to the broader upper-bound conjecture of Conjecture 0.3.2.
refined_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and for positive integers m and h define rho_hat(G,m,h) := min{|h^∧A| : A ⊆ G, |A| = m}, where h^∧A is the set of all sums of h distinct elements of A. Is it true that for every pair of integers h and m with h < m <= p, one has rho_hat(G,m,h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper-faithful target. In Section 0.1 the paper defines the restricted sumset h^∧A and the extremal quantity rho_hat(G,m,h). In Section 0.3 it first recalls the prime-order formula in Theorem 0.3.1 and then states the exact finite-abelian-group conjecture you are aiming at as Conjecture 0.3.3. The nearby sentence explicitly says that Conjecture 0.3.3 generalizes Theorem 0.3.1, confirming that this narrower conjecture, rather than the broader Conjecture 0.3.2, is the nearest official formulation of your draft. The main needed refinements are therefore definitional and quantificational, not substantive.
